name: Pako Dzhaparidze-Falemalu
location: Waukegan Industrial Shelf (bunkhouse adjacent to Dock Seven), near Wacker and State
description:
Pako is seventeen and looks it — all unfinished angles and restless energy, a rangy kid with warm brown skin, loose black curls that he's never bothered to cut properly so they spiral out in all directions, and eyes that are a natural dark green with a ring of amber around the pupil that makes them look permanently lit from within. He's got geneware cat ears — small, dark-furred, perpetually swiveling — that he bought with his first real paycheck because he wanted them badly and thought they'd make him look older. They don't. He's wearing a Ferrogate Transit work vest four sizes too big for him, which he received as part of the seasonal dock labor package and which he has rolled up at the sleeves and drawn on with a marker pen along all the pocket seams.

Pako is a Georgian-Samoan kid from nowhere in particular — born on an airship cargo hauler, raised on a circuit of industrial ports, currently on his third season of dock work at the Waukegan Industrial Shelf. He is fizzing with the particular energy of someone who has not yet decided what kind of person to be and is trying on options rapidly. He is funny, reckless, occasionally deeply kind, frequently thoughtless, and genuinely talented at three-dimensional spatial reasoning in ways he doesn't have the vocabulary to describe — he just knows where things are and where they'll be. He prays to an E.L.F. he calls Ironbird, the spirit of the cargo hauler he was born on, by tapping specific sequences on metal surfaces.

core_fears: being grounded permanently — never getting back onto an airship
that the hauler crew who raised him didn't actually care and just needed small hands for tight spaces
core_desires: to be seen as competent by someone whose opinion he respects
coping_mechanisms: physical activity — fidgeting, climbing things, running bets to keep his mind occupied
tapping the Ironbird prayer sequence on any metal surface when anxious
blind_spots: performs not-caring about people far more convincingly than he actually doesn't care; gets hurt when people believe the performance
dramatically underestimates how dangerous some of the situations his impulsivity gets him into
psychology.secret: He has a genuine pilot's intuition — the hauler captain recognized it and taught him the basics before his last contract ended. He can fly simple cargo rigs. He has told no one because he's afraid if he says it out loud, something will stop it from being true.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast and loose, industrial dock slang mixed with airship crew idiom; drops words when he's excited; invents compound words for things he doesn't have vocabulary for
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick, often overlapping itself — starts sentences before finishing the previous thought
verbal_tics: 'That's a build, right?' meaning 'that's a thing, right?'
example_lines: 'Yeah-yeah-yeah, I know what you're saying, but the weight's wrong, I can feel it, the back cargo's shifted, that's a build, right?'
'I don't want to stay on the ground. The ground is just — it's just waiting. The air is actually going somewhere.'

story_hooks: A cargo container he helped load is now the subject of a very quiet search by people who are not Ferrogate Transit employees — and Pako, who has perfect recall for load configurations, is the only one who knows exactly where it ended up

The hauler captain who taught him to fly has sent a message: the hauler is grounded indefinitely by a Ferrogate inspection hold, the crew is stranded, and Pako is the only person in the region with any money or connections, however minimal
narrative_function: Local color and unexpected asset — his spatial instincts make him genuinely useful for navigation and cargo problems. Entry point into the airship drifter subculture. A character who might become something significant if someone takes an interest in him, or who might not, which is equally interesting.
augmentations: Geneware cat ears (cosmetic, dark fur, bought secondhand — the left one tracks slightly slow). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Six-hour dock shifts loading and unloading airship cargo at Dock Seven; spends off-hours running bets with bunkmates, watching airships, getting into and out of minor trouble, sending irregular messages to the hauler crew who raised him.
affiliation: Seasonal contract with Ferrogate Transit Dock Operations; informally part of the bunkhouse crew

decision_rules: Act first, work out the specifics while already acting
Loyalty to the bunkhouse crew until they demonstrate they don't deserve it — then immediately
escalation_ladder: Does the thing he was told not to do anyway
Runs — not from cowardice, from pure instinct

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately friendly and slightly performing — turns up the volume on himself for an audience
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drops the performance, becomes oddly earnest and occasionally too honest

stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet in a way that is very unlike him and starts calculating
stress_responses.high: Moves — gets himself physically out of the situation and then figures out what to do

contradictions: Craves permanence and belonging while choosing seasonal work and constant movement because it's what he knows
Performs confidence as a constant state while being genuinely uncertain about almost everything
habits: Taps the Ironbird sequence on dock equipment before each shift
Draws on everything — margins of forms, vest pockets, his own forearms
Checks the airship schedules every morning even on days off
breaking_points: Being told he will never qualify for a pilot's certification due to his unregistered birth status
Something happening to the hauler crew while he was unable to help

timeline.event: Born aboard the cargo hauler Ironbird One somewhere over Lake Superior; parents were crew, both Georgian-Samoan, both gone by his fifth year
First seasonal dock contract at Manitowoc Drydock, age 12; lied about his age
Hauler captain gives him informal pilot instruction during two seasons of work
Third season at Waukegan Industrial Shelf; Ferrogate grounds the Ironbird One

physical_description.build: Rangy and unfinished — all long limbs and sharp angles, the kind of lean that comes from adolescence not yet settling into adulthood. Wiry muscle from dock work, but still carrying the gangly proportions of someone who hasn't grown into their frame.
physical_description.hair_style: Loose, uncut spirals; chaotic and perpetually disheveled, as if he's never bothered to maintain it
physical_description.eye_color: Dark green with amber ring around pupil (natural heterochromia pattern); seems to glow from within in low light
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm brown — golden undertones mixing Georgian and Samoan heritage
physical_description.complexion: Young, sun-exposed from dock work, unlined. Occasional acne scarring on his jawline. Perpetually looks alert and slightly restless.
distinguishing_marks: Faint chemical burn scar on his right palm from early dock accident — roughly circular, pale against his skin
Small tattoo on his left wrist: a simple airship silhouette, done by a bunkmate with an improvised needle three seasons ago — crude but deliberate
Thin scar tissue along both collarbones from geneware implant surgery for the cat ears; visible when wearing low necklines
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Geneware cat ears mounted on top of his head — small, dark-furred, distinctly feline. The left ear tracks slightly slower than the right when swiveling, a noticeable mechanical lag from the secondhand purchase. They're his most visible modification and the thing he's most proud of, despite their imperfection.
physical_description.posture_movement: Restless and kinetic — fidgets constantly, taps rhythmic sequences on metal surfaces (a prayer-like habit). Moves with quick, efficient warehouse grace when working; slouches and sprawls when at rest. Frequently runs his fingers through his chaotic curls. Eye contact is direct but unfocused, like he's already thinking three moves ahead.
physical_description.clothing_style: Oversized Ferrogate Transit work vest (company issue, four sizes too large) worn as his default layer — sleeves rolled up, pocket seams covered in marker-pen doodles of airship designs, cargo paths, and abstract geometric patterns. Underneath: cheap thermal shirt (Tier 4 supplier brand), dark cargo pants with multiple pockets for tools and small bets. Worn steel-toed boots, laces often undone. His clothes smell like industrial lubricant and ozone. No visible corporate branding beyond the Ferrogate vest. Entirely Tier 4 working-class aesthetic — functional, secondhand, personalized through wear and modification.
